speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Several Members of Parliament have also asked about the incident, and I will address their questions in my Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our healthcare family’s priorities are not just to provide good patient care, but also to safeguard the confidentiality of their data.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The attacker accessed SingHealth’s system through an initial breach on a frontend workstation, circumvented the multi-layered security barriers by using advanced and sophisticated tools, and then gained access to privileged credentials to access the database.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is not the work of casual hackers or criminal gangs, but a sophisticated and resourceful attacker.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On 4 July 2018, data administrators of our Integrated Health Information Systems (IHiS) detected unusual activity on one of SingHealth’s IT databases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: IHiS is the technology organisation that administers the IT systems for the public healthcare sector.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The immediate priority of the team was to stop the unusual activity and block the connections to prevent further access.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a result, we prevented further loss of data and no further exfiltration has been detected since 4 July.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Concurrently, the IHiS team immediately investigated the suspicious activity to determine its nature and whether it was malicious.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This process took time as our hospital systems process millions of data queries daily.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There will always be a number of unusual processes that need to be investigated and most of these turned out to be legitimate activities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Furthermore, the attacker was careful to remove its traces as it worked, making investigation harder.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On 10 July, IHiS confirmed from its investigations that it was a cyberattack, and informed SingHealth, the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the Cyber Security Agency (CSA).

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Thereafter, several streams of tasks were carried out concurrently.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: An interagency team, comprising MOH, IHiS, SingHealth, the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) and CSA, worked closely together to contain the cyberattack and undertake measures to prevent further attacks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We implemented additional containment and monitoring measures, such as restricting user access, blocking additional connections, resetting security tokens, mandating password changes for users and heightened monitoring of IT systems across our public healthcare sector.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the same time, a separate team in IHiS supported SingHealth’s efforts to assess the extent of the data affected and identify the patients these data belong to, and to plan for patient engagement to inform them of the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These included the name, National Registration Identity Card (NRIC) number, address, gender, race and date of birth.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, no phone numbers, passwords or credit card information were accessed.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: All records in SingHealth’s IT system remain intact and are unaltered.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: IHiS staff combed through detailed access logs to confirm that the databases were not tampered with.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Patient care has not been compromised and services were not disrupted during the period of the cyberattack.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On 20 July, we assessed that the situation had been stabilised and informed the public of the cyberattack, even while investigations were ongoing.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Between 20 and 23 July, SingHealth sent short message service (SMS) notifications to about two million patients who visited its healthcare institutions between 1 May 2015 and 4 July 2018, to inform them whether their personal information or medication information were affected.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: SingHealth also set up an online data check through the SingHealth website and Health Buddy application and expanded its call centres to attend to queries from patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many of our colleagues from the healthcare family were mobilised at short notice to help manage the situation and address patient concerns about the cyberattack.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This includes safeguarding the confidentiality of patient data as well as ensuring safe and effective patient care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We face the constant challenge of striking the right balance between having stronger cybersecurity safeguards, while ensuring effective and safe patient care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To achieve this, we adopted a multi-layered approach to cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our systems are designed with defensive measures against illegal access.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, there are multi-layer security defences in place, both at the perimeter guarding against threats on the Internet, as well as within the perimeter to protect against unauthorised access.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Independent IT security audits are also carried out, with the last such audit on the affected system carried out in the second half of 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have monitoring tools and services to detect breaches.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our systems are also designed to provide extensive detailed activity logs for internal and external round-the-clock monitoring.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have established operating and technical procedures and measures to contain the impact and neutralise the threat once a breach is discovered.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In the event of a breach, we will also notify and work with CSA to contain and investigate the breach.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Exercises are conducted regularly to ensure staff are familiar with the procedures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Beyond setting up a resilient system, we also need a culture of vigilance and cybersecurity awareness.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This applies to our healthcare staff, as well as our IT staff.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We should always adopt safe cyber practices, watch for suspicious emails and messages, and report them to our IT departments as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Members of Parliament have also asked about Internet surfing separation (ISS).

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Imposing ISS will limit avenues for attackers to enter and exit the healthcare clusters’ IT systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, ISS has created some inconveniences as well as operational challenges for healthcare workers and patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have taken precautions to ensure patient care and safety are not affected.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: ISS is not a decision to be taken lightly.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In fact, even before the incident, IHiS had been working with our clusters to study and assess the feasibility of ISS and the ways to mitigate the impact on patients and healthcare professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Internet access is an integral part of many of our healthcare institutions’ daily operations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They rely on the Internet to access other systems for the delivery of some healthcare services.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include receiving and reading reports from laboratories, referrals to our private sector partners, video consultation and tele-rehabilitation, as well as the payments and claims systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We were also learning from the experiences of other countries’ healthcare IT systems and exploring alternative approaches to achieve similar protection as ISS, while minimising the impact on operations and patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many healthcare systems in other countries have also found it difficult to implement ISS for practical and operational considerations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Healthcare systems, such as Hong Kong’s Hospital Authority and Kaiser Permanante have not adopted full ISS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One possible approach we are studying and piloting is the virtual browser solution.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This enables users to access the Internet more safely through a set of quarantined servers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will reduce the number of potential attack points.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The virtual browser solution will be complemented by the deployment of Advanced Threat Protection (ATP) measures, which will provide additional defence against advanced cyberattacks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our ongoing pilot on virtual browser was scheduled to be completed by September this year.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Nevertheless, given the urgency of the matter, we went ahead to implement ISS, albeit a temporary measure.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To mitigate the challenges on the ground and allow the healthcare institutions to continue to operate safely, our engineers worked overnight and through the weekend to put in place temporary work-around solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The team continues to be on the ground to resolve the problems that have arisen as a result of ISS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Areas that have been affected include reading of diagnostic reports from laboratories, video consultation and assessment of suspected stroke patients at our emergency department.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Waiting times for consultation may also be longer as doctors may need to access references on the Internet through a separate computer.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There remain some issues not yet fully resolved, such as referrals to private sector partners, and submission and retrieval of results from screening systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These do not compromise patient care and safety, but affect the efficiency of our healthcare system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a result of the security measures, some patients may experience a longer wait for consultations and in receiving their test results, as well as delays in checking their MediSave accounts or making their claims.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The productivity and efficiency of our services may also be affected in some areas.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We would like to thank our patients for their understanding as we work through these issues on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will need to develop longer-term mitigation solutions to overcome the operational issues if ISS were to stay.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Despite our security measures, the attackers had been very patient, very persistent and very resourceful.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With advanced hacking tools, they eventually succeeded in gaining access to SingHealth’s IT system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We take this seriously as there is no reason to believe that they will not try again, with even more advanced tools.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Therefore, we are reviewing the cybersecurity measures of our key IT projects and strengthening them where necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Members of Parliament have asked about the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The NEHR is a separate system that was not affected by this cyberattack.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Due to the need for the system to interface with multiple external partners, NEHR is designed differently from the systems that were infiltrated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must assure ourselves, users and patients that the necessary safeguards are in place, before we proceed with wider implementation of NEHR.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, we should not reverse our direction in the use of technology in healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Digitalisation, technology and use of data in healthcare have brought many benefits to our patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We cannot return to the days of paper and pencil.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: IT systems have allowed us to greatly improve the safety and effectiveness of patient care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: During an emergency where a patient is unconscious, access to his medical history in the NEHR helps doctors prescribe more effective medication and treatment in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Data analytics help us to better understand disease patterns and plan ahead to meet our needs in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Automation improves productivity, reduces human errors and enables patients to receive better care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: When patients receive care beyond the hospital, integration of IT systems allows easier referrals across settings and enables better team-based care, and more effective emergency response.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These have to be matched with efforts to continually improve our ability to secure patients' data, and the increasing robustness of the systems to deal with a constantly evolving cybersecurity threat.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will extend our full support to the work of the Committee.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We look forward to its report and recommendations to further strengthen our resilience against cyberattacks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will identify potential areas for improvement in cyber threat prevention, detection and response.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To do this, we will bring in third-party experts to support us in this work where necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While we have implemented additional cybersecurity measures, including the ISS, we must not be complacent and assume that we are now safe from cyberattacks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Instead, we must work on the assumption that the perpetrators will continue to try with increasingly sophisticated tools and techniques and may succeed in getting through.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must all remain vigilant, learn from this and continually strengthen our systems against evolving cybersecurity threats.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Minister for Communications and Information will be making a related Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will allow Members to raise points of clarification on both Statements after this Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: First, SingHealth's IT system was the target of a deliberate and well-planned cyberattack.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Second, this attack caused the most serious breach of personal data in Singapore's experience.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: However, their patient databases are part of our Critical Information Infrastructure (CII).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: A cyberattack on any CII can disrupt essential services and affect public welfare and confidence.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We have done a detailed analysis of this attack and have determined that it is the work of an Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) group.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This refers to a class of sophisticated cyberattackers, typically state-linked, who conduct extended, carefully planned cyber campaigns, to steal information or disrupt operations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The APT group that attacked SingHealth was persistent in its efforts to penetrate and anchor itself in the network, bypass the security measures, and illegally access and exfiltrate data.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The attack fits the profile of certain known APT groups.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But for national security reasons, we will not be making any specific public attribution.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Given the serious implications of this incident for public health and safety, I have convened a COI to get to the bottom of this incident, learn from it, and implement stronger safeguards.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will do our utmost to strengthen our cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But it is impossible to completely eliminate the risk of another cyberattack.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This is an ongoing battle, with potential cyberattackers who are constantly developing their capabilities and seeking out new vulnerabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We should not let this incident or any others like it derail our Smart Nation initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In fact, we must pursue these initiatives for they will bring benefits and opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: What matters most is that our people and systems remain resilient, that we are able to respond swiftly and effectively to a cyberattack and that we strengthen our defences and harden our systems.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I want to thank Members who have raised a range of questions on the cyberattack, our response and the COI, and I will now address them in detail.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: On 10 July 2018, CSA was notified that an unauthorised network intrusion had occurred at SingHealth.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: CSA immediately deployed members of its National Incident Response Team (NIRT) to investigate the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The CSA team conducted forensic investigations on suspected compromised computers and supported IHiS in implementing measures to contain the attack.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This included blocking unauthorised connections to prevent access by the attacker, resetting servers, enforcing mandatory password resets for all SingHealth users, heightened monitoring across all public healthcare IT systems, and implementing Internet Surfing Separation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: CSA's investigations ascertained that on 4 July, IHiS system administrators had discovered unusual activity on one of SingHealth's IT databases which triggered follow-up investigations by IHiS' IT team.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: CSA subsequently established that the attackers had obtained a foothold in SingHealth's network by infecting a frontend computer with malicious software, or what is called malware.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: No further data loss has been detected since 4 July.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The attackers also repeatedly and specifically tried to steal the medical records and data of Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Prime Minister Lee's personal particulars and outpatient dispensed medication records were stolen.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: However, to reinforce the point that Minister Gan Kim Yong made, no telephone numbers, passwords or credit card information were accessed or stolen.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Neither were other medical records, such as diagnoses, test results or doctor's notes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The data that was illegally copied was not tampered with, nor was it deleted.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: CSA has done a detailed analysis of the SingHealth cyberattack and has determined that it is the work of an APT group.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: An APT group refers to a class of sophisticated, usually state-linked cyberattackers who conduct extended and carefully planned cyber campaigns to steal information or disrupt operations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Some recent examples of cyberattacks by APT groups include the hacking of the US Democratic National Committee in 2016, and the theft of more than 20 million personnel records from the US Office of Personnel Management in 2014.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Singapore has also been the target of APT attacks, such as that on the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU) last year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The cyberattack on SingHealth had characteristics that are typical of an APT attack.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The attacker used advanced and sophisticated tools, including customised malware that was able to evade SingHealth's anti-virus software and security tools.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: After establishing a foothold in the network, the attacker took steps to remain in the system undetected before stealing the patients' information.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As the notes are being distributed, let me summarise.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It will also recommend measures to safeguard public sector IT systems containing large databases of personal data, including those in the public healthcare clusters, against similar cyberattacks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Chairman and members of the Committee have the legal, technical and operational expertise to conduct a thorough and rigorous inquiry.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Chairman, Mr Richard Magnus, was formerly the Senior District Judge, and he has chaired two other COIs before; Mr Lee Fook Sun is the former president of ST Electronics and currently Executive Chairman of Quann World, a cybersecurity company; Mr T K Udairam was formerly Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Changi General Hospital and he has decades of experience in healthcare administration; Ms Cham Hui Fong is a former Nominated Member of Parliament and Assistant Secretary General at the National Trades Union Congress.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Committee has had preparatory meetings and will soon hold its first pre-Inquiry conference.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) will lead evidence and CSA will lead a team to conduct the investigations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: After receiving CSA's investigation report, the COI will conduct the Inquiry hearings.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As some aspects of the Inquiry have security implications, the COI will decide which part of its hearings can be held in public.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Some Members have asked whether the SingHealth cyberattack could have been prevented and what are the lessons learnt.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As the COI will be addressing these issues, I seek Members' understanding to allow the Committee to conduct a thorough investigation and to complete its work without pre-empting its findings.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Meanwhile, the Government has taken additional measures to strengthen our cybersecurity defences.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: CSA's forensic investigations team has analysed the compromised computers and extracted Indicators of Compromise.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These are pieces of forensic data used to identify malicious activity on a network.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: CSA then instructed owners and regulators of CII to scan for these Indicators and advise on possible measures to mitigate a similar incident.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: CSA has also instructed CII sectors to strengthen the security around their network connectivity gateways.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In addition, the Cybersecurity Act passed by this House in February this year gives the Government additional levers to strengthen the protection of CII against cyberattacks and to respond to national cybersecurity threats and incidents.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Notwithstanding these measures, we must recognise that a balance must be struck between cybersecurity on the one hand, and operational efficiency and service quality on the other.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is a dynamic balance, one that will change as the threat landscape evolves.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: CSA will direct CII owners on the essential security measures they must adopt to meet a required standard.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Beyond this, CSA will also render its professional advice on what CII system owners could do to further strengthen their defences.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ultimately, owners and regulators of CII are responsible for ensuring the security and uninterrupted operations of the essential services they provide.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Government had taken the added precaution of calling for a pause in the introduction of new Information and Communications Technology (ICT) systems, although there was no evidence that Government ICT systems had been compromised in this cyberattack.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Smart Nation and Digital Government Group (SNDGG) was directed to review the cybersecurity measures of all existing and upcoming Government systems.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: SNDGG has completed its review and will implement additional security safeguards where necessary.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Cybersecurity is the foundation of our Smart Nation and Digital Government drive, and the Government is resolute in its commitment to strengthen our cyber defence, as well as our detection and response capabilities, in the face of the evolving cybersecurity threat.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: All organisations – not just CII operators – should take this incident as a warning to review their cybersecurity system and ensure the protection of their IT systems and databases, including personal data.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There have been concerns that the data stolen through the SingHealth cyberattack could be used for fraudulent transactions or identity theft.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I want to emphasise that there are multiple safeguards in place to mitigate such risks, especially for financial transactions and sensitive Government e-transactions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Financial institutions generally do not rely solely on personal information, like those stolen in the SingHealth cyberattack, to verify customer identity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: All banks and insurance companies in Singapore already have two-factor authentication (2FA) for online financial services, such as making fund transfers or accessing account details.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To log in, the account holder has to input his/her Personal Identification Number (PIN) and a one-time-password (OTP), received via SMS or the bank’s authentication token.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: An additional authentication layer – commonly known as "transaction signing" – protects higher-risk transactions, such as adding a third party payee or transferring large sums of money.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Unless the attacker has access to all authentication information, it would not be possible for fraudulent transactions or identity theft to occur.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Similarly, since July 2016, all sensitive Government e-transactions have been protected by SingPass 2FA.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The account holder would need to input his/her SingPass username and password, and an OTP.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Individuals can also do their part by practising good personal data protection and cybersecurity habits.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They should ensure that their passwords, user IDs and security questions are not based on personal data, use strong passwords, enable 2FA for online transactions, and watch out for fraudulent transactions and suspicious requests for personal data.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: SingCERT has published online the precautions that individuals can take in view of the SingHealth incident.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I caution the House: we cannot completely eliminate the risk of another cyberattack breaking through our defences.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ensuring cybersecurity is a ceaseless battle, like our battle against terrorism.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It involves changing technology and sophisticated perpetrators who are constantly developing new techniques and probing for fresh weaknesses.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Therefore, even as we do our best to strengthen our IT systems, it is crucial that our people and systems remain resilient, that we are able to respond robustly and decisively to an incident, and that we constantly learn and reinforce our system.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Despite this incident, or any others like it, we must press on with our plans for a Smart Nation, after learning and applying the lessons from this incident.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We must adapt ourselves to operate effectively and securely in the digital age, to deliver better public services, enhance our economic competitiveness, and create good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We have been talking about cyberattack but, practically, this has been more a case of cyber snooping or cyber theft rather than an attack, which brings me to my main question: how sure are we that no malicious malware still remains in the systems?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think we have been lucky in the sense that the systems have not been disrupted in terms of patients' safety or care.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But as I understand it – correct me if I am wrong – with this APT type of attacks, a lot of these initial attacks are meant to demonstrate that they can actually invade the systems, but the ultimate goal may be to be able to plant some malware that can disrupt our systems when the time comes.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: That was my main question: how sure are we that no malicious software remains in the systems, given that the databases is a very large and complex system.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Speaker, I thank the Member for his question.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, I do not think we should speculate on the motives of the attacker.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think it does not detract from the fact that this is an illegal criminal act and we have the responsibility to get to the bottom of it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Having said that, can we be sure that there is no remnant malicious malware in the system?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I had said earlier, our agencies –CSA working with their counterparts in IHiS and SingHealth – have done everything they can to secure the system and to detect and eliminate the risk.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Since the cyberattack, a few of my elderly residents came to see me and told me that they worry that their medication records will be altered.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we help our people, especially our elderly residents, to better understand our cybersecurity matters and even measures that will be taken?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we understand that patients will still be anxious and want to know more about this incident, and how they can protect themselves, and what implication there is for them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I encourage them to contact SingHealth which will then follow up with more detailed explanation specifically to the affected patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There is a hotline that they can call, and the number is 6326 5555.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If they want to have more details, please contact SingHealth and our people, our hotline operators, are trained to answer their questions and to help them clarify any doubts or anxiety that they may have with regard to their medication information.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have actually filed a question to the Minister for Health to ask if the Government could elaborate on the reasons for the several days of delay between the time that the attack was confirmed and the time that the public was made aware of it.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Second question is also for the Minister for Health.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: During the first press conference on 20 July, we noted that the Minister apologised for the incident.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But we are hearing today, really, that the CIIs are responsible for safeguarding the data on the systems.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, is there any significance as to why it was not SingHealth that apologised but rather the Minister who apologised?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think SingHealth, during the press conference, had also apologised, probably it was not carried in the media.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But they did apologise to the patients for the incident as well as the inconvenience that has been created.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Anyway, my apology is on behalf of the entire healthcare family.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I take it that, ultimately, I will have to apologise to the patients who are affected.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our priority at that time was to ensure that our system was protected, our data would not be subject to further exfiltration.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That took a while because, first, they had to trace back where the sources of attack came from, so that the Cyber Security staff would know where and how to protect the database.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We also need to investigate to determine whether or not there were additional data that were compromised beyond what we already knew.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, the first stream of investigation was to focus on protecting the data.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The second stream of work was on investigation of the incident to trace back to see how it started, so that we were confident that this was the only attack that we were experiencing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The third stream was to identify what were the data that were compromised and who were the patients that were affected, so that we could pave the way to inform them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, the third stream was very important as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, SingHealth also started to prepare to inform the patients, and all these will require time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In the meantime, we also had to make sure that there were no further attacks on the system.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, we have sufficient information to share with the public on how the incident happened, what were the data that were compromised, and who were the patients that were affected.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And it is important for us to ensure that our information given to the public is accurate as far as we are able to ascertain.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My second point is that cyberattacks, such as these, are actually, to me, a new form of terrorism that calls for the same, if not, more of the resources and attention that are given to, for example, physical terrorism by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I can still remember it is run-hide-tell, and many of these are things that were done to ensure that we are very cognisant of physical terrorism.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, for cyber terrorism, it is all the more important.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In view that Minister Iswaran has said that the Smart Nation plans will press on for various reasons, what is the Government's plan in terms of added resources and also acquisition of cybersecurity expertise, for example?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We know that nation-wide, there is a shortage of such cybersecurity expertise.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And so, what are we going to do about it to ensure that we are protected in the long term as we proceed with our Smart Nation plans?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We should be very clear that our challenges with cybersecurity are in no way different from our challenges with terrorism.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But when it comes to cybersecurity and defences, perhaps the level of awareness is not as palpable.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The reason is probably also because many of us, all of us, use digital devices as part and parcel of everyday life and we do not pause to think sometimes what the implications are of having this hyper-connectivity and the kind of data that flows through our devices and the connections that we have with the Internet and the wider Internet community.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, in terms of the specific question, what are we doing?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, we have to use this opportunity to reinforce the message and the importance of cybersecurity to the general public and the measures that they can take at a personal level, which is what we have just outlined, but also to organisations, public and private organisations, because often the investment in cybersecurity is seen as a cost, without an obvious payoff and value.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This sort of instances helps to crystallise why cybersecurity must be taken seriously at the top management level, and you put in place systems and make the judgement in terms of what kind of resources should be allocated for this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I said earlier, the reality is that this is going to be a ceaseless battle because the perpetrators or the potential perpetrators are constantly developing their own capabilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have many efforts in the broader ecosystem – the ICT ecosystem – and cybersecurity is one of the focal points for that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And the final point I would make is that as part of our overall defence, if you will, cyber defence, this is not just a battle we fight alone.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: All of them face similar challenges, they are all investing in their capabilities, and the cooperation with our allies helps to strengthen our own capabilities in resisting such attacks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have one clarification for Minister Iswaran and one for Minister Gan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And for Minister Gan, the Minister mentioned that the permanent ISS may be implemented for parts of the healthcare system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can the Minister elaborate which part of the system is likely to face the permanent ISS and, given that this attack happened at a frontline workstation, would this actually mean most of the healthcare systems face a risk?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In that process, I imagine that they would be looking at what could have been done, what should have been done and then, make their recommendations accordingly.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would urge Members to refrain from going down the path of allocating blame at this stage.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our resolute focus should be on ensuring that the system in SingHealth is secure and patient data is protected.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And for this, we need all parties who are involved to be working together in order to achieve that objective.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The COI will conduct its due process and, when we have the outcome of that and we know the recommendations and findings, then we can take appropriate action.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I would not want to pre-empt the decision.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We really want to understand the impact on the ground and assess which are the parts that really can continue with the ISS and which are the portions of the healthcare system that actually ISS is not practical and could affect patient care in the long term.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, just to explain, today, whilst we have introduced ISS, there are a number of workaround solutions which the IHiS team has been working with our clusters on the ground to help our doctors and patients to ensure that the system will continue.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But some of these workaround solutions are not sustainable in the long term because they are basically workarounds.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And, therefore, we will have to look at whether there are practical, long-term solutions for some of these workarounds.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In areas where it is not possible and there may be alternative safeguards that will be able to provide added protection but not necessarily ISS, those are the alternatives that we could consider.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: One example I mentioned earlier in my Statement was a virtual browser solution, together with Advanced Threat Protection measures.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And even with Internet access, there are ways to protect against our core database system.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, you could designate specific servers that they have access to and denied access to other servers that are not related.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I do not want to go into too much detail because these also have implications on our security measures.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Suffice to say that I do not want to pre-empt the outcome of the review.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We give the Committee and the team time to look at the system and to review the implementation of ISS on the ground today.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And from the experience of ISS, we can then make an informed assessment of which are the parts that should continue with ISS and which are the parts we should maybe refer to alternative solutions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In relation to the COI's Terms of Reference No 5, I noticed that the focus is largely on public sector IT systems.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am aware that the COI's Terms of Reference are, in particular, on public health data.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Maybe the Minister can share a bit more on that, in particular, for example, telecommunications companies, banks and private hospitals, and what is the plan, strategically, for CSA to address some of these issues.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Member then asked whether there are issues around databases and IT systems that reside outside the public sector.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Some of these sectors the Member highlighted are banking, telecommunications.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is where, as I mentioned in my earlier Statement, CSA will ensure that there are certain minimum requirements that are implemented.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But beyond that, there may also be certain advisory guidelines on what else they can do to further strengthen cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But ultimately, the regulators and owners of those CIIs will have to make the judgement call and be accountable for the uninterrupted essential services they provide.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the point of the private sector, what we learned from this incident will be shared.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have various platforms to do that in because there are, generally, various education sessions that Government agencies conduct to heighten awareness of cybersecurity and the measures that can be taken.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We also have the frameworks of the Personal Data Protection Act and the Personal Data Protection Commission which are actively involved not just in following up on complaints or reports of personal data breaches but also in terms of raising awareness and education and sharing best practices, so that the general private sector can also continue to harden itself against cyberattacks.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: If that is the case, then may I know whether the Government knows which state is behind the attack or is linked to this attack?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: And, if so, whether or not the Government is prepared to share the knowledge with Singaporeans on which state is carrying out such an attack on us.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: In the details, Minister Iswaran mentioned that the attack was conducted by a professional group, APT Group.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Does the Government or CSA in its investigations, know what is the name of the Group and where this Group has launched the attack from?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: And the Minister also mentioned that data was copied to another server.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: So, may we know where is the server sited?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Member asked whether we are prepared to share the names, if we know specifically who, and whether we are able to then share that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would put to the Member that, first, I have explained why we have a larger set of concerns around this matter.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And this is the kind of evidentiary threshold that may not stand up in a Court of law but, at the operational level, the agencies that are involved have a high level of confidence in their findings.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Having said that, we do not think it serves our national interest, nor is it a productive exercise for us to be making specific public attribution.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many of my residents expressed concern when they heard that their personal details had been stolen, especially of NRIC.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They are very worried and they do not know how this data will be used later on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, it is not just about the ID, although in some cases, and I think, in many cases, the IC number is used as the ID.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And this might be an opportunity for us to review that and see whether we can use other IDs which are more robust.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And then, in addition to ID, you need the password as well as the one-time password.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the point the Member made about alerting them to any other kind of activity which can have financial implications, typically, in all of these transactions, you would have to not just put in your IC number or name.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If you are going to, for example, buy something online, you need either credit card data or some other kind of financial information.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That information has not been taken in this instance and, therefore, that link is broken.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Hence, the consumers and the general residents can be comforted by that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But we should not get complacent and we should review this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And where they have got some accounts, it is well worth using this opportunity to look at resetting passwords.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I believe Minister Iswaran mentioned that this has many analogies to a terror attack.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And certainly, in dealing with the terrorists, the Government does have powers, for example, under the Internal Security Act, to investigate and detain without evidence that would stand up in a Court of law.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And the national security reason is why you would not want to put it in the Court of law.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Does the Minister think we need similar frameworks to deal with cyber threats?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think our existing legislative framework provides us with sufficient scope, because if you can demonstrate and prove a criminal act, then you can take action under the Penal Code or appropriate legislation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But this is a domain where the nature of the crime and specific attribution can be quite challenging at times.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: After the conclusion of the COI process, will MCI or other relevant authorities attempt to reach out to cybersecurity and IT professionals across the whole-of-Government and, indeed, in the private sector, to apprise them of some of the findings, to educate them maybe about the signatures of some of these groups that have made the attacks so that they can be better alerted to detect and pre-empt them, and also educate them on some of the preventive measures that they should undertake, drawing on the learnings from not just this attack, but perhaps the one at NUS and NTU as well that happened previously?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But the qualifier I will make is that what we can share is constrained by the considerations I had pointed out earlier.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But they do need to take up certain basic measures for cybersecurity purposes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But the larger point about drawing lessons which can then be shared, this is something that we certainly intend to do.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As IT talents are global and, as part of our cyber defence, I would like to ask the Minister if the Singapore Government Ministries, Organs of State and Statutory Boards and agencies have in place bug bounty programmes to tap upon the global expertise of white hats or ethical computer hackers, and if the compensations for their effort and time are globally competitive.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I understand where the Member is coming from.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: My question is for the Minister for Communications and Information.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: While we regret this incident in SingHealth, can the Minister enlighten us whether other countries are also victims of cyberattacks?

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Is it to see if any crimes have been committed?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, have other countries been victims of cyberattacks?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In my Statement, I highlighted a couple, both of which are in the context of the US.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But there have also been other incidents in Europe.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I think many of these may not even be reported in the public domain, but we know that they are occurring.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, the truth of the matter is that this is a universal challenge; we are not an exception.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, every country is facing this challenge and the greater their connectivity and the use of digital technologies, the greater their challenge as well.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, that is an important point that all of us need to understand and appreciate.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It will be aided by CSA, which leads a team of investigators, and they will also have the AGC leading evidence.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Police report was lodged because there was suspicion of a crime being committed.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And so, the Police will investigate this incident in that context.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And they, too, are conducting their own investigations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And again, they too, will take reference from what is being conducted within the COI hearing process as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My sense, after hearing what the Minister said in the Statement, is that we are really at the mercy of these state-linked cyberattackers, almost to operate on their terms.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I want to ask the Minister whether besides the defensive measures that we take, are there any counter-offensive measures that we can also take as part of cybersecurity strategy so that we can not only defend but also deter such attacks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First of all, I think we should not create the impression that we are helpless or that we are at the mercy of these potential perpetrators.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If that was the case, then why have this strong robust response?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And so, we must have that resilience that when it happens, we will pick ourselves up again and we will learn from it, grow stronger and we will carry on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that is the most important aspect of the way we can deter such attacks.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will take the Chair at 4.35 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.14 pm until 4.35 pm.
